text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal did enough to make the halfway cut despite a triple bogey eight as Bernhard Langer climbed into the lead early in the second round of the Desert Classic on Friday.

A frisky breeze known locally as a "shamaal" blew in off the Persian Gulf and made it a day for marking time on the 7,102-yard Emirates course, and Olazabal continued his comeback from crippling foot problems to play steadily except for the 18th hole, his ninth.

A triple bogey eight including a fourth into the lake following a missed drive more than cancelled out two earlier birdies but he recovered well for a 74 to stand one under par after his opening 69, his first round after an 18-month injury break.
He is one under par with the cut expected to fall at one or two over at the end of the round.
"I played as well as yesterday apart from one hole. I'm going to ask the sponsors if I can just play 17 holes tomorrow," he said.
"At the 18th I missed the drive but I played it solidly otherwise. It was just one of those things.

"But I'm happy to be playing at the weekend. I'm still just going to go out and try to score well. No I'm not thinking about winning the tournament. You don't think about that until the final afternoon."
Olazabal, who began his round at the 10th, reached five under par with birdies at his fourth and eighth holes before his drive at the next finished in the trees.
His recovery got through the nearest trees but then hit a palm tree and dropped to the base of the trunk from where he could only play out sideways.
He tried a seven iron to get over the lake "but the wind was stronger than I thought and held the ball up. I felt I struck it well," he said.
After a penalty shot, he pitched on and two-putted.
Two holes later he dropped another shot but seven successive pars closed out his round.
"Except for the 18th, I played very solidly. Taking the wind into consideration, it was much tougher than yesterday," he said.
Langer collected three early birdies and held on for a two- under-par 70 to move past joint overnight leader Colin Montgomerie, the holder and his playing partner.
The Scot shot 16 pars and a single birdie at the 17th hole, his eighth, before dropping his first shot of the tournament at his last hole, the ninth, for a level-par 72.
Langer moved to eight under par with Montgomerie on seven under, still level with co-overnight leader Domingo Hospital who had not begun his round.
Neither had world number one Greg Norman, who in the windy conditions might be hard-pressed to improve on his disappointing opening effort of 71.
Langer had his streak of winning at least one European Tour event a year ended after 16 years in 1996, though he captured the Alfred Dunhill Masters after the tour season ended.

He is now a convert to the broomhandled putter pioneered in Europe by Sam Torrance and it helped him sink putts of 15 and 12 feet for birdies. He also looked confident on the short putts, holing out well right through his round.
The third member of their group, Irishman Padraig Harrington, also shot 72 to stay on six under par.
The trio were collectively 19 under par in the first round. On Friday they were two under.
